**Annabella Avery Thorne** (born October 8, 1997) is an American actress, singer, and writer. Thorne gained prominence for her role as [CeCe Jones] on the [Disney Channel] series _[Shake It Up] "Shake It Up (American TV series)")_ (2010–2013), for which she received several awards and nominations, including winning an [Imagen Award].[[2]] Thorne has since appeared in numerous feature films, including _[Blended] "Blended (film)")_ (2014), _[Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Road Chip]_ (2015), _[The Babysitter] "The Babysitter (2017 film)")_ and [its sequel] (2017–2020). She received praise for her roles in _[The DUFF]_ (2015), _[Amityville: The Awakening]_ (2017), and _[Infamous] "Infamous (2020 film)")_ (2020). Thorne also led the drama series _[Famous in Love]_ (2017–2018), for which she received nominations from the [Teen Choice Awards].

Outside of acting, Thorne has ventured into music; she released her debut single, "[Watch Me] "Watch Me (Bella Thorne and Zendaya song)")" in 2011, which charted at No. 86 on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100]. She has since released the EP _[Made in Japan] "Made in Japan (EP)")_ in 2012 and the EP _[Jersey] "Jersey (EP)")_ in 2014. She made her directorial debut in 2019, directing the [pornographic film]_[Her & Him]_, which garnered positive reviews and won a [Pornhub] Visionary Award.

In September 2017, Thorne revealed that she had lived in a suburban area, spoke Spanish as her first language, and that she was bullied while growing up because she was [dyslexic].[[15]][[16]] She was diagnosed with dyslexia while in first grade. She was home-schooled after previously attending a public school, where she had been bullied. She improved in her learning after attending a [Sylvan Learning] center and began reading and writing a grade ahead.[[17]] In April 2010, she said she had overcome dyslexia by rigorously reading everything she could find, including cereal box labels.[[18]][[19]]
